function.mechanism: Provides hydrogen ions to reduce pH and control/neutralize formulation acidity.
common_food_categories: foods and beverages requiring pH adjustment

adi.basis: EFSA FAF 2019 used a human chloride reference value (not a classical ADI) for risk assessment.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded exposure to chloride from E507/E508/E509/E511 does not raise a safety concern at reported use and use levels; high-percentile exposure in some younger groups was slightly above the reference value.

fda.notes: GRAS when used as a buffer and neutralizing agent in accordance with good manufacturing practice.

concerns.summary: EFSA noted some animal evidence suggesting chloride may contribute to increased blood pressure, but considered human data more appropriate for deriving a reference value.
High-concentration hydrochloric acid ingestion is corrosive and can cause severe multiorgan injury and death in poisoning/case-report contexts.
Case literature reports acute tubular necrosis after concentrated hydrochloric acid ingestion.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA summary reports no concern for genotoxicity and carcinogenicity in the evaluated chloride additive group.
JECFA lists ADI as not limited for hydrochloric acid.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported slight exceedance of the 40 mg/kg bw/day chloride reference value at the 95th percentile in some younger groups; mean exposures were below or at the reference value.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory evaluations (EFSA/FDA/JECFA) support safety at intended additive use levels, while severe harms are linked to concentrated corrosive exposures rather than normal dietary exposure. Slight high-percentile exceedance of EFSA's chloride reference value in younger groups justifies caution but not escalation to high concern.
key_factors: EFSA 2019 no-safety-concern conclusion at reported use levels
High-concentration ingestion toxicity not representative of food-additive exposure
